links.title: 4. More Control Flow Tools — the else clause on loops
links.why: Worked prime-number example showing a loop's else running only when the loop finishes without break.

links.title: 4. More Control Flow Tools — the range() function
links.why: Tutorial section showing range with one, two and three arguments, including negative steps.

links.title: 8. Compound statements — the while statement
links.why: Exact grammar of while, with its else clause and how break and continue behave.

links.title: 8. Compound statements — the for statement
links.why: States that the loop runs until the iterator is exhausted, then runs the else suite.

links.title: Built-in Types — Ranges
links.why: Explains that a range is an immutable sequence storing only start, stop and step, so it uses constant memory.

links.title: Built-in Functions — enumerate
links.why: Reference for enumerate(iterable, start=0) returning count and value pairs.

links.title: Built-in Functions — zip
links.why: Reference for zip, which stops at the shortest input and raises ValueError with strict=True on unequal lengths.

links.title: 7. Simple statements — the break statement
links.why: Break ends the nearest enclosing loop, skips the else clause and runs any finally first.

links.title: 7. Simple statements — the continue statement
links.why: Continue jumps to the next cycle of the nearest enclosing loop, running any finally first.

links.title: sys — System-specific parameters and functions (sys.exit)
links.why: sys.exit raises SystemExit, its argument sets the exit status, and finally clauses still run.

links.title: 7. Simple statements — the import statement
links.why: Lists every import form and says the wildcard form binds public names and is allowed only at module level.

links.title: 6. Modules
links.why: Tutorial on import, from-import and import * with a warning that import * hurts readability.

links.title: 5. Data Structures — Looping Techniques
links.why: Advises building a new list instead of changing one while looping over it, and shows enumerate and zip.

links.title: PEP 572 – Assignment Expressions
links.why: Shows the := operator in while loops, removing the need for a separate assignment before the loop test.
